title: M-C Garchomp Three-Mode
lede: Garchomp-centered M-C six: Primarina + Gholdengo as the balance core, Salamence / Golisopod / Mimikyu as flex. Preview decides Garchomp’s job — Mega breaker, Scarf revenge, or Sash lead — then the other two.
philosophy: Garchomp is not one standardized Pokémon in M-C. Roughly seven in ten ladder Garchomps sit in three different offensive identities. Build a toolbox that can support whichever job their six demands — do not paste “Stealth Rock physical Chomp” onto every game.
meta: Season M-6 Singles (as of 2026-09-16, Champions Battle Data): Garchomp is #2 overall behind Salamence. Regulation M-C newly legalized Garchompite Z alongside Mega Salamence, Mega Lucario, and Mega Golisopod. Only one Mega per battle. Golisopod sits #5 on this CBD snapshot (some Zone views still show it #4 — same cluster either way).
setsNote: 66 SP, max 32. Default roster Garchomp is Mega teaching mode (Garchompite Z). Scarf and Sash are first-class preview modes on the same registered species — change the item with the three, not mid-ladder panic.

evidence.source: Champions Battle Data Singles + Pokémon Zone M-C coverage
evidence.caveat: Item shares below Mega are ordered from CBD but not all rows expose exact percentages in our snapshot. Zone’s ~19.6% Scarf / ~16.8% Sash match the second and third slots we see. Early season — treat as construction evidence, not proven best WR.

stats.label: Garchompite Z
stats.note: Largest single item mode — Mega breaker is real, not mandatory.

stats.label: Scarf / Sash / other
stats.note: Choice Scarf and Focus Sash are the clear #2/#3 identities on CBD; Sitrus and Rocky Helmet follow.

stats.label: Earthquake
stats.note: Only move near universal. Stealth Rock is common but far from mandatory.

stats.label: Top spread
stats.note: 27.3% on CBD. Special lines (Draco, Earth Power, Flamethrower) prove mixed/special Chomp is not a gimmick.

stats.label: Rough Skin
stats.note: Ability is not the ambiguity — item and attacking side are.

stats.label: Top mates
stats.note: Then Lucario, Baxcalibur, Archaludon. Gholdengo (#9) and Mimikyu (#11) are deliberate glue/flex adds.

construction.thesis: Start with Garchomp + Primarina + Gholdengo, then hold Salamence, Golisopod, and Mimikyu so the six can support Mega, Scarf, or Sash Garchomp without weather or mandatory Rocks.
construction.method: Read Garchomp as a three-mode Pokémon first, then pair clusters: Primarina for Water/Fairy insurance, Golisopod for 3v3 priority finishes, Salamence for Mega ambiguity, Gholdengo for Fairy resist + special plot, Mimikyu for Disguise anti-offense. Skip auto-adding Baxcalibur (Dragon overlap + shared Fairy hole) and skip forcing Archaludon into a rain story.
construction.winCondition: Preview → name Garchomp’s job (break / revenge / guarantee a lead action) → pick item/mode → bring the two partners that cash that job.

substitutions.why: Bax is #7 and a real mate, but stacking Dragon/Ice offense next to Garchomp doubles the Fairy hole without fixing priority or Disguise. Mimikyu gives emergency setup and anti-HO insurance the balance six actually needs.
Lucario is a top mate and a strong special Mega — but this six already carries Salamence as the alt Mega. Gholdengo covers Fairy without competing for the stone as hard, and still Plots.

altSlots.why: When you want maximum Mega ambiguity (Chomp / Mence / Lucario) and will accept less defensive glue.
Steel special attacker that is not Fairy-immune the same way — use when their six makes Archaludon’s profile better than Good as Gold, not because you drifted into rain.
Raw Ice/Dragon pressure into bulky cores — only if you accept more Fairy vulnerability and less Intimidate Mega ambiguity.

megaPool.rule: One Mega per battle. This six registers Garchompite Z and Salamencite — Golisopite stays off the registered stones so Golisopod can keep Emergency Exit utility unless you consciously swap.
megaPool.previewPressure: They see Garchomp + Salamence and must guess which stone is live. Scarf or Sash Garchomp removes that guess on purpose — that is also a preview tell you can choose to send.

candidates.when: Their six is Ground-weak, lacks a clean physical wall, or you need the Mega breaker to crack a structure.
Dragon Dance into their midrange is cleaner than Mega Chomp, or you want Intimidate into physical offense while Chomp is Scarf/Sash.

pilot.thesis: Garchomp’s item is a preview decision equal to the three. Primarina and Gholdengo are the default glue; Salamence, Golisopod, and Mimikyu exist so Mega, Scarf, and Sash modes all have partners.
pilot.rule: Name Chomp’s job before you name the lead. Do not click Stealth Rock because “Garchomp teams set Rocks.”
pilot.fail: Lock Garchompite Z every game and bring the same three into HO that needed First Impression day one.

press: Force them to respect Mega, Scarf, and Sash Garchomp from the same registered name.
Use Primarina Encore to create windows for Dance or Swords Dance.
Finish weakened targets with Golisopod or Mimikyu priority — Chomp does not have to sweep alone.
refuse: Never treat Stealth Rock as mandatory (~EQ is the only move near 2/3 usage).
Never Mega Salamence and Mega Garchomp the same battle.
Never leave Chomp in on Fairy without Gholdengo or a Disguise plan.

plan.title: Preview
plan.goal: Decide Chomp’s mode and which Mega stone (if any) is live.
plan.play: Mark Speed tiers, Fairy answers, and whether you need a guaranteed lead action. Assign Mega / Scarf / Sash, then pick the three.
plan.next: Lead the partner that enables that mode — not the partner you practiced most.

plan.title: Pressure
plan.goal: Put something into KO range for priority or the Mega breaker.
plan.play: EQ / special coverage from Chomp, Encore from Primarina, Plot from Gholdengo, First Impression or Shadow Sneak to finish.
plan.next: If the mode was wrong, change item next game — keep the six.

plan.title: Close
plan.goal: Convert chip without donating the wincon to Fairy or Ice revenge.
plan.play: Gholdengo holds Fairy; Primarina handles Dragons; Mimikyu Disguise buys the last setup turn when needed.
plan.next: Scarf mode cleans; Mega mode breaks; Sash mode already spent — don’t ask it to wall.

switches.send: Gholdengo — Steel resists; Make It Rain answers.
Golisopod First Impression or Mimikyu Disguise.

victims.name: Electric / Steel midrange
victims.why: Ground STAB plus Primarina Fairy forces awkward switches.

victims.name: Physical Balance without Fairy
victims.why: Mega or Scarf Chomp + Gholdengo Plot outlasts one wall.

victims.name: Glass HO
victims.why: Golisopod / Mimikyu priority packages deny free turns.

counters.name: Double Fairy + Ice
counters.why: Chomp and Salamence both suffer — lean Gholdengo/Primarina and consider Scarf revenge over Mega Dance.

counters.name: Bulky Water/Fairy cores
counters.why: EQ alone stalls — need special Chomp lines or Lucario/Archaludon alt slots.

counters.name: Priority Dark into Mimikyu
counters.why: Disguise is not immortality — don’t lead Mimikyu into known Sucker Punch without a plan.

advantages.title: Three-mode preview
advantages.body: Mega, Scarf, and Sash are different Pokémon that share a sprite on their six. Exploit that before the lead drops.

advantages.title: Hazards optional
advantages.body: Earthquake is the constant. Stealth Rock is a package tool — bring it when chip helps Mimikyu/Golisopod finishes, skip it when the three needs coverage instead.
advantages.play: Sash lead Rocks is a mode, not a religion.

loops.title: Chip → First Impression
loops.body: Garchomp puts a name into range; Golisopod finishes. Chomp does not need the KO.

loops.title: Encore → Dance / SD
loops.body: Primarina Encores a Protect or setup turn; Mega Chomp or Salamence converts the free turn.

loops.title: Disguise → Shadow Sneak
loops.body: Mimikyu eats one hit, then priority cleans what Chomp or Golisopod softened.

hazards.title: Fairy on Chomp
hazards.body: Dragon/Ground hates Fairy. Gholdengo is the registered answer — if it’s not on the three, don’t force Mega Chomp into Moonblast.
hazards.rule: No Fairy answer on the three → different pack or Scarf revenge from a safer slot.

hazards.title: Ice into Dragons
hazards.body: Salamence + Garchomp share Ice pain. Primarina and Mimikyu are the insurance — don’t bring Double Dragon into double Ice.
hazards.watch: Choice Scarf Ice and priority Ice.

roster.title: The Three-Mode Ace
roster.role: Primary wincon whose item defines the game. Default teaching set is Mega; Scarf and Sash are equal preview identities.
roster.itemWhy: 35.3% CBD — largest single mode. Teaching default for “break their structure.” Swap to Scarf or Sash when preview says so.

itemAlts.name: Choice Scarf
itemAlts.why: Second ladder identity — revenge and Speed control when Mega is wrong.

itemAlts.name: Focus Sash
itemAlts.why: Third ladder identity — guarantee Rocks or a hit into HO / revenge.

training.label: Fast physical Mega
training.why: Top CBD spread shape (2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe). Special-oriented training lives on the mixed Mega / coverage sets below.
spend: 32 Spe — race midrange before or after Mega.

alts.name: Mixed / special lean
alts.why: When Draco Meteor / Earth Power / Flamethrower are the plan — SpA investment matches the large special share Zone reports and the move mix CBD shows.

moves.name: Earthquake
moves.why: ~67% CBD. The constant — Ground STAB into Electric, Fire, Steel, Rock.

moves.name: Dragon Claw
moves.why: Reliable Dragon STAB without Outrage lock — default Mega physical line.

moves.name: Rock Slide
moves.why: Flying / Fire / Ice coverage; flinch value in 3v3.

moves.name: Swords Dance
moves.why: Mega breaker conversion when Primarina or Mimikyu buys the turn.

roster.objective: Break, revenge, or guarantee a lead action — pick one before the timer ends.
roster.howToPlay:
On preview, assign Mega, Scarf, or Sash.
Do not default Stealth Rock — only when the package wants chip.
Earthquake is the button; coverage and setup change with the mode.
If Fairy is healthy and Gholdengo is benched, you picked the wrong three.

modes.label: Mega Garchomp
modes.when: Their six is Ground-vulnerable or needs a high-power flexible attacker, and you are willing to spend the Mega.
modes.itemWhy: 35.3% — primary ladder mode. Mega also enables special investment more cleanly when you run mixed lines.
modes.objective: Crack the defensive structure; do not play like a hazard lead.
modes.howToPlay:
Mega when the breaker job is clear.
SD only after Encore, Disguise, or a forced switch.
Mixed sets swap Dragon Claw / Rock Slide for Draco / Earth Power / Flamethrower / Power Gem when their walls are physical.

modes.label: Choice Scarf
modes.when: Their six has several threats you cannot outspeed otherwise, or Salamence/Golisopod wants the Mega stone more.
modes.itemWhy: Clear #2 ladder identity. Locks you into one move — pick the revenge target in preview.

training.label: Scarf revenge
training.why: Max Speed Attack for locked Earthquake / Outrage lines.

moves.name: Outrage
moves.why: Dragon nuke when you accept the lock — Dragon Claw if you need flexibility.

moves.name: Fire Fang
moves.why: Steel that walls EQ — Flamethrower if special lean.

modes.objective: Be the fast answer after chip — not the lead setup piece.
modes.howToPlay:
Bring when Speed tiers scare you.
Do not lead Scarf into known resist walls.
Pair with Primarina/Golisopod so something else creates the chip.

modes.label: Focus Sash
modes.when: You need Rocks, a trade, or a hit into something that would otherwise OHKO — and the Mega stone is elsewhere or unused.
modes.itemWhy: Clear #3 ladder identity. Guarantees Garchomp does its job once.

training.label: Sash utility
training.why: Offense first — Sash is the bulk.

moves.name: Stealth Rock
moves.why: The main reason to be Sash lead — chip for Mimikyu/Golisopod.

modes.objective: Guarantee something happens on the lead turn.
modes.howToPlay:
Lead when HO or revenge would delete un-Sashed Chomp.
Click Rocks if the package wants them — skip if you needed coverage instead.
After Sash breaks, you are glass — hand off.

roster.title: The Foundational Pair
roster.role: Water/Fairy balance glued to Garchomp. Covers Ice/Dragon/Fire pain; Encores windows for Chomp’s mode.
roster.itemWhy: Keeps Encore and Aqua Jet online after chip.

training.label: Fast special
training.why: Pressure Dragons and land Encore first.

moves.name: Moonblast
moves.why: Fairy STAB into Dragons — Chomp’s partner answer.

moves.name: Aqua Jet
moves.why: Priority finish when Golisopod is benched.

roster.objective: Be the insurance half of Garchomp + Primarina.
roster.howToPlay:
Switch into Dragons and Fire.
Encore Protect and setup.
Do not soft-click into Electric without Chomp ready.

roster.title: The Fairy Net
roster.role: Steel/Ghost glue and special Plot. Fixes Chomp’s Fairy problem without turning the six into sand walls.
roster.itemWhy: Blocks the first Ground; spend it deliberately.

moves.name: Nasty Plot
moves.why: Second setup path while they watch Chomp.

roster.objective: Hold Fairy and force special answers.
roster.howToPlay:
Come in on Moonblast aimed at Chomp.
Plot when revenge is gone.
Balloon is one Ground — play like it.

roster.title: The Other Stone
roster.role: Intimidate + Dragon Dance + Mega ambiguity with Garchomp. Often the correct Mega when Chomp is Scarf/Sash.
roster.itemWhy: Second stone on the six. Preview pressure next to Garchomp is half the value.

moves.name: Dragon Dance
moves.why: Setup wincon when Mega Mence is the stone.

roster.objective: Be the Mega when Dance beats Mega Chomp’s breaker job.
roster.howToPlay:
On preview with Garchomp, force the stone guess.
If Chomp is Scarf/Sash, Mence is often the Mega.
Don’t Dance into Ice.

roster.title: The Finisher
roster.role: 3v3 priority. Puts the game on a timer after Chomp chips — First Impression / Sucker Punch / U-turn.
roster.itemWhy: This six already registers two Mega stones on Chomp/Mence. Keep Golisopod as Emergency Exit priority glue unless a pack explicitly wants Golisopite.

itemAlts.name: Golisopite
itemAlts.why: When you bench Salamencite and want Tough Claws Mega priority instead of Emergency Exit.

training.label: Bulky priority
training.why: Live to Exit and keep First Impression relevant.

moves.name: U-turn
moves.why: Hand Chomp or Primarina in with tempo.

roster.objective: Finish what Garchomp starts — Chomp does not have to sweep.
roster.howToPlay:
Bring anti-offense packs.
First Impression the name you came for.
U-turn into Intimidate or EQ pressure.

roster.title: Disguise Insurance
roster.role: Emergency setup and anti-offense. Disguise buys the turn Sash Chomp or Dance needs.
roster.itemWhy: Pay HP for KO power after the costume breaks — Sitrus if you want safer Shadow Sneak wars.

itemAlts.name: Sitrus Berry
itemAlts.why: Bulkier priority cleaner into longer games.

training.label: Priority cleaner
training.why: Maximize Shadow Sneak / Play Rough after Disguise.

moves.name: Swords Dance
moves.why: Convert Disguise into a sweep turn.

moves.name: Play Rough
moves.why: Fairy STAB into Dragons that bother Chomp.

moves.name: Shadow Claw
moves.why: Ghost STAB when Sneak is predicted.

roster.objective: Be the emergency button against HO and revenge chains.
roster.howToPlay:
Bring with Golisopod/Chomp into fragile sixes.
Disguise once — spend it on Dance or a KO.
Don’t donate into known priority Dark for free.

packs.label: Balance core
packs.when: Midrange sixes without a hard HO open or double Fairy wall.
packs.identity: Learn the foundational Garchomp + Primarina + Gholdengo relationship.

strategy.opponentPattern: Balanced or mildly offensive structures Ground can crack.
strategy.purpose: Default teaching three — Fairy net, Water glue, Mega breaker.
refuses: Pure HO needing First Impression day one
strategy.winCondition: Chip or Encore into Mega EQ / SD pressure while Gholdengo holds Fairy.

pilot.thesis: This is the first package to learn — not every-game autopilot.
pilot.rule: Mega Chomp only when Fairy is answered.

packs.philosophy: Foundational relationship first; flex packs later.

packs.label: Anti-offense
packs.when: HO-shaped sixes — glass, Sash, early KOs.
packs.identity: Chomp pressure + Golisopod priority + Primarina bulk/Aqua Jet.

strategy.opponentPattern: Hyper Offense or fragile Balance that needs the first turn.
strategy.purpose: Deny momentum — First Impression and Aqua Jet finish what EQ starts.
strategy.winCondition: Chip into priority; Sash Chomp if you need a guaranteed lead action.
strategy.winconMode: Focus Sash lead (or Mega if they lack Fairy)

pilot.thesis: Chomp does not sweep — it puts names into Golisopod range.
pilot.rule: Lead Golisopod or Sash Chomp, not Dance Chomp.
pilot.fail: Leading Mega Chomp into their revenge chain.

packs.label: Mega ambiguity
packs.when: Higher-level opponents who respect both stones.
packs.identity: Garchomp + Salamence stone guess with Gholdengo on a third axis.

strategy.opponentPattern: Sixes weak to Ground or to Dragon Dance — you pick after preview.
strategy.purpose: Force Mega ambiguity while Fairy is covered.
strategy.winCondition: Correct stone + Gholdengo Plot or Recover glue.

pilot.thesis: The guess is the advantage — don’t waste it by auto-Mega Chomp.
pilot.fail: Mega the wrong Dragon into their prepared answer.

packs.label: Maximum offense
packs.when: You accept less glue for three offensive axes.
packs.identity: Chomp + Salamence + Mimikyu — pressure and Disguise without Primarina.

strategy.opponentPattern: Passive or slow sixes that lose to continuous offense.
strategy.purpose: Aggressive bring — Scarf Chomp revenge while Mence or Mimikyu sets up.
strategy.winCondition: Disguise or Dance window into Scarf cleanup.

pilot.thesis: Offense over glue — only when their six can’t punish Fairy holes.
pilot.fail: Playing this like the Primarina balance package.

packs.label: Priority pressure
packs.when: You want to deny free attacks into HO.
packs.identity: Chomp chip + Golisopod First Impression + Mimikyu Disguise/Sneak.

strategy.opponentPattern: Hyper Offense that lives on free turns.
strategy.purpose: You don’t get to freely attack — priority and Disguise everywhere.
strategy.winCondition: Sash Rocks or EQ chip into First Impression / Shadow Sneak.

pilot.rule: Disguise is one hit — spend it.

refuse: Letting them set up for free
